messages:

Subject: DPIA & LLM training data questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the intro — BrightCare is finishing our vendor DPIA for any vendors that expose LLM-powered endpoints. We have a few targeted questions about how Redwood handles customer prompt/response data and whether that data could be used to improve models. Can you confirm the following for our evaluation?

1) Does Redwood use customer prompts or responses (from the Hosted API) to train, fine-tune, or improve any shared models or production weights by default?
2) What is the default retention window for prompt/request bodies and generated responses for Hosted customers?
3) Can customers opt-out of their data being used for improvements, and if so what is the exact process & timeline to apply an opt-out?
4) Who at Redwood has access to raw prompt/response logs (SRE, Support, Research)? Are there documented access controls and audit logs?

If possible, could you attach any DPIA/summary document and a simple data flow diagram that we can include in our controls workbook? We need this by end of week to keep our procurement timeline.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump on a short call if that's easier.

Best,
Maria
Senior Information Security Manager
BrightCare Health

Attachments: none

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPIA & LLM training data questions

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. I've summarized our position and attached a short DPIA-ready package (redwood-dpia-summary.pdf) plus a data flow diagram. High-level answers below; see the attachments for more detail and controls references.

TL;DR: We do not use customer prompts/responses from Hosted accounts to continually update or re-train shared base models unless a customer explicitly opts in to an "improvements" program or signs a model-training addendum. For Hosted API customers, default behavior is logging for troubleshooting, caching, and rate-limiting only.

Answers:
1) Training/use for improvements: NO by default. Customer data from the Hosted API is not fed into training pipelines for our public/shared models without explicit customer consent (opt-in). Dedicated and Private deployments are isolated and treated per contract (data does not leave customer-dedicated capacity).

2) Retention windows: Default retention for prompt/request bodies and generated responses is 30 days for Hosted accounts (used for troubleshooting, billing, and abuse detection). After 30 days we purge request/response payloads from primary stores. Derived telemetry (metrics, aggregated latency/cost) is retained in summarized form for longer.

3) Opt-out process: Customers can enable a "data opt-out" flag from the Console or via an API call (Accounts API: POST /v1/accounts/{id}/preferences with "use_for_improvements": false). Once set, the opt-out is effective immediately for future data and we apply backfill removal processes for retention stores; full backfill purge completes within 72 hours for active caches and 30 days for archived/backup stores. We included a short snippet of the opt-out processing steps in opt-out-process-snippet.txt.

4) Access controls & audit: Access to raw prompt/response data is strictly limited to authorized Support and SRE engineers for incidents and billing investigations, and to a small set of Security engineers when required. Research/Model teams do NOT have routine access to production prompts/responses. All access requires justification and is recorded in our audit log (we can provide filtered audit extracts on request).

Attachments included: redwood-dpia-summary.pdf (DPIA summary + high-level controls), data-flow-diagram.png (simplified flow), opt-out-process-snippet.txt (API examples + runbook steps). Also linking a shared drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/DP-2321/llm-evidence.

If you want, we can apply a tenant-level opt-out for BrightCare as a one-time operation while legal finishes the contract — tell me the account id and I'll initiate the request. Happy to review the DPIA with your team on a call; I can loop in Neha (privacy counsel) and Markus (head of infra).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpia-summary.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); data-flow-diagram.png (PNG, 220KB); opt-out-process-snippet.txt (TXT, 4KB)

- For the opt-out backfill you mentioned: does the 72-hour purge window cover all hot caches across regions, or is that per-region? We need assurance that replicated caches will also be cleared within that timeframe.
- Access audit evidence: could you provide a redacted example of an access audit entry showing a justification, approver, and timestamp (so our reviewers can see the format)?

Also, legal asked about SCCs for international data flows — we'll include that in a follow-up if necessary, but for now the DPIA team wants the cache/opt-out/audit items answered.

Would appreciate a short response (or the specific artifacts) by tomorrow EOD PST.

Maria

Maria — quick follow-up with clarifications and next steps. Quoting your questions below.

> Can you confirm whether any short-term caches ... could be sampled by internal processes for model tuning or research?

No — the inference runtime's KV caches and prefix caches are used purely for in-flight performance optimization and are not part of any training pipeline. Those caches are ephemeral and cleared on instance restart; we do not extract cached entries into training datasets. Research teams are explicitly blocked from accessing caches; only on-call SREs may access an instance for debugging, and access is logged and time-limited.

> For the opt-out backfill: does the 72-hour purge window cover all hot caches across regions?

We enforce the 72-hour window across active regions for Hosted accounts. Our backfill job coordinates with region replicas; hot caches are signalled to invalidate within minutes and region-level purge completes within 72 hours. We documented the orchestration steps in the runbook excerpt included in the shared drive.

> Access audit evidence: could you provide a redacted example of an access audit entry showing a justification, approver, and timestamp?

Attached is a redacted audit sample (in the Drive link) showing a Support access request flow: requestor, ticket id, justification, approver id, and start/end timestamps. If your team needs the sanitized CSV extract, we can produce that under an NDA.

Next steps:

- I'll schedule a 30-minute call with Neha (privacy counsel) and Markus (infrastructure) to walk your DPIA reviewers through the attached artifacts — proposed time: Thu 2026-03-25 10:00 AM PST.
